sources.title: Maharashtra State Gazetteers: Satara, Later Chalukyas
sources.note: Read indexed original government gazetteer. Taila II overthrow of Rashtrakutas in 973 to 974; succession, Kalyani, Vikramaditya VI and later fragmentation. Do not repeat its erroneous attribution of Mitakshara to Bilhana or inconsistent 1128 date. Map period starts are display subdivisions, not new state foundations.

sources.title: Archaeological Survey of India, Dharwad Circle: Lakkundi temples and sculpture gallery
sources.note: Direct read. Attimabbe and Brahma Jinalaya in 1007, literary patronage, chloritic schist and specific animal carvings. Page has inconsistent monument counts and editing boilerplate, omitted here. The thousand copies are the remembered donation, not a surviving manuscript census.

sources.title: J. F. Fleet, Dambal inscription no. CXVI, and J. Burgess correction, Indian Antiquary 10 (1881)
sources.note: Direct original edition OCR read, printed pages 185 to 190; Burgess correction pages 273 to 274 explicitly identifies Buddhism, correcting Fleet’s erroneous Jain identification. Date Saka 1017, 1095 to 1096. Sample at printed page 185, translation 187; modern macron normalization of published Roman transliteration. No original Kannada glyph facsimile claimed. Unknown commodities and ambiguous levy denominations omitted.

sources.title: Gérard Colas (2023), Palm-leaf Manuscript Libraries in Southern India Around the Thirteenth Century
sources.note: Full author research article text read, printed pages 142 to 143, notes 28 to 31. Specifically the Nagai 1058 Kannada inscription, despite the article’s broader thirteenth-century focus. Six librarians, 200 Veda and 52 shastra students, land allocations, food and accommodation. Underlying 1928 inscription edition not independently fetched. Omit uncertain engraved total 257 versus corrected 267. DOI 10.1515/9783110779653-007; alternate publisher/OAPEN access failed.

sources.title: Saumya Gupta (2025), Cookbook Chronicles: Documenting Cooking in Hindu Households, PMML Occasional Paper 114
sources.note: Direct full PDF read, printed pages 15 to 16, chapter on Lokopakara. Supports 1025 Kannada practical compendium and chapter 8 with 57 verses, lacking precise measurements/durations. Do not reuse anomalous chilli reference, author’s sectarian identification, or disputed individual recipe identifications. No claim that prescriptions describe every household.

sources.title: Maharashtra State Gazetteers: Ratnagiri, Later Chalukyas
sources.note: Indexed original passage read. Kharepatan 1008 grant was made by tributary Rahu Raja/Ratta Raja, not the Chalukya sovereign personally. Krishnamandi village granted to Avveshvara temple for feeding ascetics, learned men and visitors.

sources.title: Karnataka Tourism: Gadag, Lakkundi heritage description
sources.note: Indexed original tourism authority page read. Lakkundi stepwells, specifically Musukina Bhavi by Manikeshwar Temple. No exact construction year or generalized sanitation claims. Do not use this page’s confused description of the Dambal Buddhist foundation as a jinalaya.

proposedOverrides.name: Western Chalukyas
proposedOverrides.summary: The Western Chalukyas continued from Kalyani into the twelfth century, when Kalachuri, Yadava and Hoysala powers reshaped the Deccan.

batchIdentityNotes.identity: The imported 1000 to 1100 record is assigned to the Western/Kalyani Chalukyas, not the earlier Badami dynasty.
batchIdentityNotes.limitations: Single coarse 1000 snapshot covers a broad peninsular zone; it is not a century-long stable boundary. Public overview and ending distinguish imported window from dynasty chronology. No aliases added. Detailed evidence is local to named institutions, not generalized empire-wide.
batchIdentityNotes.writingWitness: Fleet 1881 printed page 185 has Namo Buddhaya, with translation Reverence to Buddha! on page 187. Unicode macron is an explicitly normalized transliteration. Burgess pages 273 to 274 corrects Fleet’s conflation of Buddhism and Jainism.

batchIdentityNotes.note: Exact indexed 1100 to 1200 continuation of the same Western Chalukya dynasty represented by chalukya-empire in 1000 to 1100. Shared detailed card expanded through the twelfth century; imported polygons unchanged.
